title: Police say fatal shots fired in self-defence ; Constables will tell their version of events to SIU: [Ontario Edition]
article: Two Toronto police officers will sit down with civilian investigators today and tell their version of what happened the night John Menga was shot to death.
Constables Paul Lentsch and Bobby Grewal will tell the special investigations unit that they acted in self-defence on Feb. 1, their lawyer says.
"We're pushing the two Cs- courtesy and co-operation," said lawyer Gary Clewley. "They were doing their duty, and they intend to demonstrate it."
The provincial unit probes all serious injuries or death involving police in Ontario.
Lentsch and Grewal were identified as the subject officers in the SIU's probe into Menga's death.
Subject officers are those whose conduct appears to have caused a death or serious injury.
The witness officers in this case- those who saw what happened- have already been interviewed by the SIU.
In the past, subject officers have often been reluctant to be interviewed by the SIU and have used their constitutional right to remain silent.
Clewley said he thinks the officers in this case should talk to SIU investigators because they did nothing wrong and want to clear the air.
Witnesses have said that Menga, who was driving a stolen Jeep with a passenger inside, was shot when he drove toward the two police officers who had ordered him to stop.
Police sources told The Star that Menga and the passenger had just purchased crack cocaine near Bloor and Havelock Sts. when the two police officers saw them around 9: 55 p.m. on Feb. 1.
Menga's wife Rosa has said her husband, the father of her two young children, was a good man, a good dad. She said she believes he "panicked ... and was scared" when he saw the officers.
Despite his criminal record, which included drug offences, the 29- year-old Menga was no longer involved with drugs and was employed as a seasonal construction worker, his wife said.
Lentsch has almost five years on the job, while Grewal has been with the force for six months.
